docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
My subsystem measures obstacle distance and controls the left-to-right motion of the LiDAR sensor. A PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano communicates with the TFmini-S sensor and controls the scan motor through a DRV8833 motor driver. An encoder tracks rotation, and a home switch establishes the starting reference position. The planned total sweep is between 90 and 180 degrees.

The battery is located inside the handle. The Power Board provides battery charging and converts the nominal 9 V battery supply to regulated 5 V. A local regulator supplies 3.3 V to the controller and encoder. The scanning board communicates with the Data Collection Board through J2 using 3.3 V UART signals.

My Top 3 Options for Slip Rings

Solution Pros Cons Option 1.* Slip Ring with Flange - 22mm diameter, 6 wires, max 240V @ 2A$14.95/each*link to product * Lower no-load current reduces battery demand; smallest stall-current requirement; integrated encoder supports closed-loop position control; compact and lightweight. *Mounting flange with holes makes it easier to attach to a stationary bracket. *Supports up to 300 RPM, comfortably above your motor's 108 RPM no-load speed. *Six independent channels provide two extras beyond the sensor's four connections. *Adafruit provides a manufacturer datasheet and dimensional information. *Gold-plated contacts and 2A current rating per channel. * The most expensive option, almost reaching your $15 budget before shipping.*Larger 22mm housing and approximately 44mm flange take up more space.*Does not have a hollow center for your motor shaft.*I2C communication reliability is not guaranteed. Option 2.* 22mm 6 Wires 6 Conductors Capsule Compact Slip Ring 220V AC 250Rpm CCTV Monitor * $7.99/each * Link to product * Cheapest option, leaving approximately $7 of your budget for mounting materials.*Supports continuous rotation at up to 250 RPM.*Six channels, with two available as spares.*Gold-plated contacts.*Listing specifies electrical noise and operating-temperature information.*Listed flange diameter of 44.5mm makes bracket mounting possible. * Lower maximum speed than the other two, although still sufficient for your motor.*Larger than the miniature eBay option.*Short 150mm leads may require cable extensions.*No verified I2C compatibility.*May require additional testing and documentation for your engineering report. Option 3.* 12.5mm 300rpm 6 Wires CIRCUITS 2A Capsule Slip Ring AC 240V Motor Robotics * $13.42/each * Link to product * Smallest option, with a 12.5mm diameter and 15mm body length.*Lightweight, compact housing is attractive for a handheld LiDAR device.*Six electrical channels.*Supports up to 300 RPM.*24mm flange diameter takes up less room than the other two options.*Listed with free shipping. *Unbranded product, with less confidence in long-term consistency and documentation.*Smaller flange may require more careful bracket design.*Greater difficulty accessing or securing wiring in a compact enclosure.*No verified I2C reliability.*Seller's published specifications would need to be checked against the actual delivered part.

Choice: Option 1: Adafruit 22mm Flanged Slip Ring with 6 Wires, 2A per Channel (Part #736)

Rationale: The Adafruit 22mm Flanged Slip Ring is the preliminary selection for the LiDAR scanning subsystem because it provides a balance between electrical connectivity, rotational speed capability, mounting convenience, and reliability. Its six independent electrical channels allow the Holybro VL53L1X sensor to maintain power and I²C communication through continuous 360-degree rotation without twisting the connecting wires.

Compared to smaller slip-ring alternatives, the Adafruit model offers a larger mounting flange, making it easier to secure within the scanning assembly. Its 300 RPM maximum rotational speed exceeds the motor's expected operating speed, while its 2A-per-channel rating provides sufficient current capacity for the sensor's electrical connections.

The slip ring also provides two additional channels for potential future expansion. Its published specifications and mounting dimensions make it a promising candidate for integration into the handheld LiDAR device. Final selection will depend on mechanical mounting compatibility, available enclosure space, and testing the reliability of I2C communication during continuous rotation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is designed to control the rotational movement of a 360-degree LiDAR scanning system. The subsystem uses a 25SG-370CA-78-EN DC gear motor with an integrated encoder to rotate the LiDAR sensor continuously while tracking its angular position.

The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano serves as the main controller, sending signals to a FAN8100N H-bridge motor driver to control the motor's movement. The encoder provides feedback to the microcontroller, allowing the system to monitor rotational speed and estimate angular position.

The schematic also includes a 5V linear voltage regulator (LM7805), power filtering capacitors, a fuse, debugging components, and connectors for communication with other team subsystems. The motor driver requires a separate, compatible motor supply.

This subsystem will support the team's overall LiDAR system by providing continuous rotational movement and encoder feedback for coordinating distance measurements.

Figure 1: Showing a example schematic.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this power budget is to determine the electrical requirements of the Motor and Rotation Control subsystem for Team 105's Handheld LiDAR Accessibility Aid.

The subsystem uses a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller, a Pololu 100:1 Medium-Power Micro Metal Gearmotor (Part #5138) with an integrated quadrature encoder, and a DRV8833 motor driver.

The power budget identifies the voltage and current requirements of these components, considers the necessary voltage regulation, and evaluates the power needed to operate the scanning mechanism.

A 25% safety margin is included when determining the required current capacity of the power supply. mkmklms

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text:
The power budget identifies the electrical requirements of the selected scanning motor, integrated encoder, motor driver, and microcontroller.

The selected Pololu #5138 motor has a nominal operating voltage of 6 V and a stall current of 670 mA at its rated voltage. The motor's supply voltage must be coordinated with the team's Power Board to ensure compatibility with the final design.

The power budget will be updated as the remaining electrical specifications, regulator selections, and battery requirements are finalized.
